An illustrative story.
Northstar Technologies, Berlin.Fictional company, design targets

“Are we doing enough?” Four weeks from a quote for forty hours to a signed readiness statement.

A 40-person software company wants to expand into Italy and France. A prospect asks for NIS2 readiness and a position on the EU AI Act. A law firm quotes forty hours just to understand the setup.

Northstar Technologies is a fictional company. The numbers in this story are the targets Regulift is designed around, not measured results.

Day 1Connect

Northstar connects GitHub, AWS, their HR platform and CRM with read-only credentials and uploads the policies they have. No interviews, no spreadsheet. By the afternoon, Regulift has mapped fourteen systems, six third-party processors and three models that make decisions about people.

Day 2Understand

Two personal-data flows to a US analytics vendor were never documented. One scoring model falls into the AI Act's high-risk category for employment. The cloud setup already meets most NIS2 controls, but there is no incident procedure on paper. Regulift turns this into an inventory, an evidence list and eleven concrete actions, ranked.

Weeks 1 to 3Improve

The team works the list: a processing agreement with the vendor, a retention schedule, an incident playbook, a human-oversight note for the scoring model. Regulift re-reads the systems and marks each item as evidenced. Nine of eleven actions close without a lawyer.

Week 4Review

The partner law firm receives an organised evidence pack instead of a blank page. They review the high-risk classification and the two remaining open items, and sign off on a readiness statement. Northstar answers the procurement questionnaire the same week and keeps the deal.

  • 14systems mapped on day one
  • 11 → 2open items left for the lawyer
